questions.question: A sum of ₹ 5000 is invested for two years under compound interest at 10% p.a, interest being compounded annually. The interest earned (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 5000

Rate = 10%

Time = 2 years 

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1+r/100)t 

C.I = A - P

**Calculations :**

**Substituting the values in formula **

A = 5000(1+10/100)² 

A = (110 × 110)/2

⇒ A = 12100/2 

⇒ A = Rs.6050

C.I ⇒ A - P = 6050 -5000

**∴ C.I = Rs. 1050**

questions.question: What is the fourth proportional to 3, 7 and 15?
questions.solution:
**Given :**

let x be the fourth proportional of 3,7 and 15 

then 3 : 7 :: 15 : x 

**Concept Used:**

If a : b :: c : d

then ad = bc

d = bc/a

**Calculation:**

3/7 = 15/x

⇒ x = (15 × 7) / 3 

⇒ x = 35

**∴ Fourth proportional of 3, 7 and 15 is 35**

questions.question: The speed of train in going from Bhopal to Varanasi is 100 kmph while when coming back from Varanasi to Bhopal, its speed is 80 kmph. What is the average speed during the whole journey? (correct to two decimal places )
questions.solution:
**Given**

**Speed of train are 100 m/hr and 80 m/hr**

**Formula **

average speed 2× (xy)/(x y)

where, x and y are speed of the train

**Calculation**

Average speed = 2 × (100 × 80)/(100 + 80)

⇒ 16000/180 = 88.89

**∴ Average speed is 88.89 m/hr**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a cistern in 20 minutes whereas the cistern when full can be emptied by a leak in 28 minutes. When both are opened,the time taken to fill the cistern is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Pipe A can fill a cistern in 20 minutes

The leak can empty it in 28 minutes 

**Calculation**

By LCM method

⇒ LCM of 20 minutes and 28 minutes = 140

⇒ Efficiency of Fill pipe = 140/20 = 7 unit

⇒ Efficiency of leaked pipe = 140/28 = 5 unit

⇒ When both pipes are opened efficiency = 7 - 5 = 2 unit

**∴ Cistern fill in 140/2 = 70minute**

questions.question: What is the difference between A’s and C’s total marks in the exam?
questions.solution:
Given: the difference between A’s and C’s total marks in the exam

Marks obtained by A in Mathematics = 88

Marks obtained by A in Science = 86

Marks obtained by A in English = 66

Marks obtained by C in Mathematics = 72

Marks obtained by C in Science = 68

Marks obtained by C in English = 84

Calculation:

Total marks obtained by A in all subjects together = marks obtained by A in Mathematics + marks obtained by A in Science + marks obtained by A in English 

⇒ Total marks obtained by A in all subjects together = 88 + 86 + 66

⇒ Total marks obtained by A in all subjects together = 240

Total marks obtained by C in all subjects together = marks obtained by C in Mathematics + marks obtained by C in Science + marks obtained by C in English 

⇒ Total marks obtained by C in all subjects together = 72 + 68 + 84

⇒ Total marks obtained by C in all subjects together = 224

∴ the difference between A’s and C’s total marks in the exam = Total marks obtained by A in all subjects together - Total marks obtained by C in all subjects together

⇒ 240 - 224

⇒ 16

**Hence, the difference between A’s and C’s total marks in the exam is 16.**

questions.question: A dice is rolled two times. Find the probability of getting a composite number on first roll and a prime number on second roll?
questions.solution:
**Calculation**

Number of composite number in a dice are (4 and 6)

⇒ Probabilty of composite number in a dice = 2/6 = 1/3

⇒ Number of prime number in a dice = 2, 3 and 5

⇒ Probability of prime number in a dice = 3/6 = 1/2

**∴The probability of getting a composite number on the first roll and a prime number on the second roll = 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6**

questions.question: John travels 2/3rd of a distance by bike and remaining 6 km on foot. How many km does he travels in the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

John travels a distance by bike =(2)/(3)rd of the total distance 

John travels a distance by foot = 6 km

**Calculation:**

Let us take the total distance traveled be x

John travels a distance by foot = x - (2)/(3) x ⇒ (1)/(3) x -----------------------(I)

John travels a distance by foot = 6 km -----------------------(ii)

Equating (I) and (ii)

6 = (1)/(3) x

x = 18 km 

**∴ The total distance traveled = 18 km**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Unitary Method Approach:

Distance travelled by Bike = 2/3

Total Distance = 3 units

That means, 2 units out of 3 units travelled by Bike

Remaining Distance travelled by Foot = 1 unit (given as 6 km)

1 unit = 6 km

3 units = 6 × 3 = 18 km

questions.question: A person purchases a silk cloth of length 50 m and width 1 m at the rate of ₹ 250 per sq m and a cotton cloth of length 40 m and width 2 m at the rate of ₹ 200 per sq m. What is the difference between the prices of two cloths?
questions.solution:
**Given**

A person purchases a silk cloth of length 50 m and width 1 m at the rate of ₹ 250 per sq m and a cotton cloth of length 40 m and width 2 m at the rate of ₹ 200 per sq m

**Calculation**

Area of silk cloth = 50 × 1 = 50 sq m

⇒ Rate of silk cloth = 50 × 250 = Rs.12500

Area of cotton cloth = 40 × 2 = 80 sq m

⇒ Rate of cotton cloths = 80 × 200 = Rs.16000

So, the difference between the prices = Rs. (16000 - 12500) = Rs. 3500

**∴ The difference between the prices is Rs. 3500.**

questions.question: Sixty percent of the rats included in a particular experiment were female rats. If some of the rats died during the experiment and 30% of rats died were male, what was the ratio of the death rate among the male rats to the death rate among the female rats?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Female rat in particular experiment = 60%

Male rats in particular experiment = 40%

Female rats died in experiment = 70%

Male rats died in experiment = 30% 

**Calculation:**

Let the number of rats be x 

The number of female rats = 60% of x = 0.6x 

Number of male rats = 40% of x = 0.4x

Let the number of rats that died be y 

The number of female rats died = 70% of y = 0.7y

Number of male rats died = 30% of y = 0.3y

Death rate of male rats = (0.3y)/(0.4x) = (3y)/(4x) ----(I)

Death rate of female rats = (0.7y)/(0.6x) = (7y)/(6x) ----(II)

The ratio of the death rate among the male rats to the death rate among the female rats

⇒ (3y)/(4x) / (7y)/(6x) = {18 over 28} = 18 : 28 = 9 : 14

**∴ The **ratio of the **death rate of male to female rats is 9 : 14 **

questions.question: If a man cuts the grass of a lawn in T minutes, what part of the lawn can he cut in 30 minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

the grass of a lawn is cut by a man = T minutes

**Concept used:**

If a person does work in n days,

then one day work by a person = 1/n part of the total work.

**Calculation:**

∴ Grassland will be cut by a man in 1 minute = 1/T part

⇒ In 30 minutes, Grassland will be cut by a man = (1/T) × 30 part

⇒ In 30 minutes, Grassland will be cut by a man = 30/T part

**Hence, part of the lawn can be cut in 30 minutes is 30/T.**
